en.name: Fufu flour
en.summary: Fufu flour is dried cassava, yam or cocoyam milled to an instant pounding flour. It is almost pure starch with hardly any fat, so it keeps well as long as it stays dry: about 6–12 months in a sealed jar in a cool cupboard. That figure is read across from white flour, since no source publishes one for fufu.
en.pantry: Keep it airtight, cool and away from the stove, where it runs 6–12 months. Humidity is the only real enemy: a low-fat starch flour does not go rancid the way a legume or whole-grain flour does, so what ends it is moisture. A bag that has caked into lumps or smells musty has taken up water and should go — a dried food that reabsorbs moisture in storage is not rescued by drying it out again, and any visible mould means the lot goes. Fermented cassava fufu flour smells sour when it is perfectly fresh; that is the ferment, not spoilage, and it is worth knowing which kind you bought.
en.fridge: No refrigerator timeline is published for fufu flour and it does not really need one — a dry cupboard covers the realistic life of a bag. In a very humid climate a genuinely airtight container in the fridge is a reasonable precaution, provided you let it come back to room temperature before opening, so condensation forms on the container rather than in the flour. Reconstituted fufu dough is a different food: it is a cooked starch, so it goes into the fridge within two hours and is eaten within a few days.
en.freezer: No freezer figure is given for fufu flour. Freezing a sealed bag is a practical way to deal with pantry insects in a bulk purchase, but it is not a documented shelf life and this page will not turn it into one. Cooked fufu can be wrapped in portions and frozen, and that is the more useful thing to put in a freezer, though again no published figure is offered here.
spoilage: Caking into hard lumps that do not break up — the flour has taken up water.
A musty or mouldy smell, as distinct from the normal sour smell of a fermented cassava flour.
Any visible mould, including specks in the corners of the bag.
Weevils, small moths, webbing or fine dust in the packet.
tips: Decant the bag into an airtight jar the day you buy it.
Store it away from the sink and the kettle; steam is what ruins it.
Learn the smell of your fermented flour when fresh, so you can tell sour from musty.
Refrigerate reconstituted fufu promptly and eat it within a few days.

faq.q: How long does fufu flour keep?
faq.a: About 6–12 months in an airtight jar in a cool, dry cupboard. The figure is borrowed from white flour.

faq.q: Why does my fufu flour smell sour?
faq.a: Fermented cassava fufu flour smells sour when fresh — that is the ferment. A musty or mouldy smell is different and means it took up moisture.

faq.q: Does fufu flour need to be refrigerated?
faq.a: No, a sealed jar in a cool cupboard is enough. Cooked fufu dough, on the other hand, must be refrigerated promptly.

zh.name: 富富粉
zh.summary: 富富粉是把樹薯、山藥或芋頭乾燥後磨成的即食搗泥用粉。它幾乎是純澱粉、幾乎不含油脂，所以只要保持乾燥就很耐放：密封裝罐、放陰涼櫥櫃約 6～12 個月。這個數字是比照白麵粉讀過來的，因為沒有任何來源替富富粉公布過期限。
zh.pantry: 密封、陰涼、遠離爐火，大約 6～12 個月。濕氣是唯一真正的敵人：低脂的澱粉粉類不會像豆類粉或全穀粉那樣走油耗，真正終結它的是水分。結成硬塊或聞起來有霉味，就代表它已經吸了水，該丟了——乾燥食品在保存中重新吸濕，不是再烘乾一次就能救回來的，而且只要看得到霉就整包丟棄。另外，發酵型的樹薯富富粉在最新鮮的時候就帶酸味，那是發酵不是腐敗，所以先弄清楚你買的是哪一種很重要。
zh.fridge: 富富粉沒有公布的冷藏期限，實際上也不太需要——乾燥的櫥櫃已經涵蓋一包粉的實際使用期。在非常潮濕的氣候，用真正密封的容器放冰箱是合理的預防措施，但開封前要先回到室溫，讓水氣凝在容器上而不是粉裡。至於調好的富富麵糰，那是另一種食物：它是熟澱粉，兩小時內要進冰箱，並在幾天內吃完。
zh.freezer: 這裡沒有給富富粉的冷凍數字。把密封袋冷凍是處理大量採購時櫥櫃害蟲的實用做法，但那不是有出處的保存期限，本頁不會把它寫成一個數字。煮好的富富可以分份包好冷凍，那才是比較值得放冷凍庫的形式，只是同樣沒有可引用的公布數字。
spoilage: 結成撥不開的硬塊——代表粉已經吸水。
聞到霉味（要和發酵樹薯粉本來的酸味分清楚）。
看得見任何霉，包括袋角的小斑點。
袋內有米象、小蛾、絲網或細粉屑。
tips: 買回來當天就倒進密封罐。
遠離水槽和熱水瓶；蒸氣才是毀掉它的元凶。
先記住自家發酵粉新鮮時的味道，之後才分得出「酸」和「霉」。
調好的富富要盡快冷藏，並在幾天內吃完。

faq.a: 密封裝罐放陰涼乾燥的櫥櫃約 6～12 個月。這個數字借自白麵粉。

faq.q: 我的富富粉為什麼有酸味？
faq.a: 發酵型的樹薯富富粉新鮮時本來就帶酸味，那是發酵。霉味是另一回事，代表它受潮了。
不需要，密封罐放陰涼櫥櫃就夠了。但調好的富富麵糰必須盡快冷藏。
